title: Placement v1
description: The frozen placement record of an IGZ level, as produced by src/igz/model-resolve.mjs. A placement is a header-table record carrying a transform, an optional behaviour script and an optional model reference. Its class index is per file and is detected structurally (finding igz.types.per-file-indices), never hardcoded. Every attribute is accompanied by the evidence that produced it: a value obtained from the runtime fixup map of a booted level is not the same claim as a value read from the file structure alone. Frozen on 2026-09-13; a later revision must be published as placement-v2.

offset.description: file offset of the placement record; it is a header-table entry

span.description: bytes from this record to the next header-table entry; a replacement must match it exactly

behavior.description: record referenced by +0xA8, named by its .ai path; null when the placement runs no script

field.description: offset of the field that resolved the model; 0xDC in every case observed so far

path.description: .mdl path, read from the model record's +0x08

model_candidates.description: every model record reachable from the placement; more than one entry with status ambiguous

layers.description: names of the header-table records that reference this placement, excluding its own blob, other placements, and .ai/.mdl records. On the tutorial this rule keeps 1170 words of which 100% are runtime pointers, and recovers every layer the runtime-based implementation reported.

users.description: number of placements resolving to this model record

rewritten_by_replacing.description: offset of the placement whose blob physically holds the model record; replacing that blob rewrites the model for every user

status.description: model resolution status, repeated at the top level for filtering

layout.description: which finding the field offsets come from and how far it is proven

evidence.description: runtime-pointer: the word is in the level's runtime fixup map, so the game rewrote it at load. structural: only the file's construction supports it. structural-only: the structural reader claims a pointer the runtime map does not confirm.
